headings.title: Maintenance of Missouri state museum and exhibits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1943/1949 history note, and footnote referencing Reorganization Plan No. 12 of 1976. Directs the department of natural resources to maintain a conservational and historical Missouri state museum displaying state natural resources and products and to install exhibit equipment.

headings.title: Appointment and duties of state museum director
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and history/reorganization notes. Requires the department of natural resources to appoint a state museum director with duties and responsibilities directed by the department.

headings.title: Capitol museum space and soldiers' and sailors' memorial hall
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and section notes. Directs the board of public buildings to designate first- and second-floor capitol space for the Missouri state museum, including a wing or section designated as the Missouri soldiers and sailors' memorial hall.

headings.title: Coordination with board of public buildings on capitol space
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and section notes. Requires department coordination with the board of public buildings regarding use of capitol corridors, halls, walls, and other space for museum and memorial hall displays.

headings.title: Receipt of military records, inscriptions, and tablets
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and section notes. Directs the department to receive from the adjutant general all matters and records pertaining to Missouri soldiers, sailors, and Marines serving in all wars declared by the United States, including desirable and available inscriptions and tablets.

Confirmed agency roles (DNR, board of public buildings, adjutant general) and capitol/memorial hall distinctions; retained all five titles and tightened subsection 5's reviewNote to match the exact statutory phrase 'wars declared by the United States'.

headings.title: Art museum board contracts to furnish facilities or services
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1963 history note. Authorizes an art museum administrative board of control to contract to furnish use of its institution's facilities or services to any incorporated city, incorporated village, school district, or county, or its citizens or residents, whether or not the subdivision maintains an art museum.

headings.title: Authority of specified political subdivisions to contract
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1963 history note. Authorizes any incorporated city, incorporated village, school district, or county to contract with an art museum administrative board of control for facility or service use by or for the benefit of its citizens or residents.

headings.title: Compliance with sections 70.210 to 70.230 and contract terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1963 history note. Requires contracts under section 184.015 to comply with sections 70.210 to 70.230 and define the nature and extent of facility or service use and compensation.

headings.title: Authorized funding sources for contract payments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1963 history note. Authorizes paying contracted amounts from general revenues of a city, village, or county or from a school district's incidental fund, out of available funds.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and 1963 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Checked covered entities (incorporated cities, incorporated villages, school districts, counties, and their citizens/residents), sections 70.210 to 70.230 compliance, and available-fund payment sources. Revised subsections 1 and 2 to avoid over-generalizing counterparties or unnamed political subdivisions; retained subsections 3 and 4.

headings.title: Required contents of museum property notices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(6), 1991 history note, and December 31, 1991 effective date. Lists six baseline items required in every notice given by a museum under sections 184.101 to 184.122 in addition to notice-specific content.

headings.title: Restricted certified mail delivery and deemed notice date
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1991 effective-date note. Requires mailing museum notices by restricted certified mail to the lender's or claimant's last known address of record and deems notice given on receipt if proof of receipt arrives within thirty days of mailing.

headings.title: Notice by newspaper publication and museum location rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1991 effective-date note. Authorizes two consecutive weekly newspaper publications in both the museum's and the lender/claimant's county or city when identity, address, or thirty-day proof of receipt is unavailable, sets notice date as the second publication, and defines museum location including branch loans.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including subdivisions (1)-(6), 1991 history, and December 31, 1991 effective-date note, and verified all fingerprints. Checked restricted certified mail delivery, thirty-day proof-of-receipt condition, newspaper publication fallback, and principal-office versus branch location rules. Retained all three titles as accurate and properly qualified.

headings.title: Emergency conservation or disposal of loaned property without notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(3), 1991 history note, and December 31, 1991 effective date. Permits conservation or disposal without permission or formal notice, absent a contrary written loan agreement, when immediate action is needed to protect property or address a health/safety hazard and one of three contact/response conditions applies.

headings.title: Museum cost lien and conditional liability protection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including lead-in, subdivisions (1) and (2)(a)-(b), and 1991 effective-date note. When a museum acts under this section or with lender/claimant agreement (unless the loan agreement provides otherwise), grants a lien on the property and any disposition proceeds for costs and bars liability for injury or loss if the museum held a reasonable belief of necessity and exercised reasonable care.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions (1)-(3) and (2)(a)-(b), 1991 history, and December 31, 1991 effective-date note, and verified all fingerprints. Verified contrary written loan agreement exceptions, lender/claimant-agreement trigger, disposition-proceeds lien, and dual reasonable-belief/reasonable-care liability conditions. Retained both titles and expanded subsection 2's reviewNote.

headings.title: When museum may give loan termination notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(2), 1991 history note, and December 31, 1991 effective date. Allows notice of intent to terminate a loan after seven years of museum custody without written lender contact for indefinite loans, or after expiration of a fixed-term loan held at least seven years.

headings.title: Required statutory statement in loan termination notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text including indented notice form and 1991 effective-date note. Prescribes substantial statutory language informing recipients they have ninety days to contact the museum in writing, establish ownership, and arrange collection or be deemed to have donated the property.

headings.title: Museum acquisition of title after ninety-day nonresponse
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1991 effective-date note. Provides that the museum acquires title to loaned property if the lender or claimant fails to file a notice of intent to preserve interest within ninety days after the date of the last termination notice.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including subdivisions (1)-(2), quoted statutory notice form, 1991 history, and December 31, 1991 effective-date note, and verified all fingerprints. Checked seven-year custody thresholds for indefinite versus fixed-term loans and ninety-day nonresponse title acquisition. Retained all three titles as accurate and distinct.

headings.title: Eligibility to acquire title to undocumented property
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1991 history note, and December 31, 1991 effective date. Permits a museum to acquire title by notice to undocumented property held in its custody for at least seven years without valid claim or written contact in its records.

headings.title: Required statutory statement in title acquisition notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text including indented notice form and 1991 effective-date note. Prescribes substantial notice wording describing the property and warning that failure to make written contact within ninety days waives ownership claims.

headings.title: Incontestable museum title after ninety-day nonresponse
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1991 effective-date note (retaining archived 'property on loan' phrasing inside this undocumented-property section). Makes museum title incontestable under section 184.116 if no notice of intent to preserve an interest is filed within ninety days after the last notice.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including quoted statutory notice form, 1991 history, and December 31, 1991 effective-date note, and verified all fingerprints. Checked seven-year undocumented-property conditions, section 184.116 incontestability cross-reference, and retained source phrasing 'property on loan' in subsection 3. Retained all three titles and documented the subsection 3 phrasing in its reviewNote.

headings.title: Filing deadline, two-year duration, expiration notice, and renewal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1991 history note, and December 31, 1991 effective date. Sets a ninety-day written filing deadline (deemed filed on receipt), clarifies filing does not revive extinguished claims, establishes a two-year effective period with thirty-day post-expiration restricted certified mail notice, and permits two-year extensions.

headings.title: Required contents of notice of intent to preserve interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(4) plus 1991 effective-date note. Requires adequate property description, ownership documentation, truth attestation, and signature under penalty of perjury.

headings.title: Noncompliant notices, amended filings, and retention effect
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1991 effective-date note. Relieves museums from retaining noncompliant notices, permits notifying claimants of insufficiency, allows filing an amended notice within the later of remaining filing time or twenty days after notification, and clarifies that retention under section 184.121 does not concede sufficiency or effectiveness.

headings.title: Director rulemaking for standard preservation notice form
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1991 effective-date note (retaining archived reference to 'subsection 1' requirements alongside contents in subsection 2). Directs the director (defined in section 184.102 as director of the department of economic development) to adopt by rule a standard preservation notice form facilitating recordkeeping and recording museum receipt and return of receipt copies.

headings.title: Effective date for sections 184.101 to 184.114
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and 1991 history note. Sets December 31, 1991 as the effective date for sections 184.101 to 184.114.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections including subdivisions (2)(1)-(4), 1991 history, and December 31, 1991 effective-date note, and verified all fingerprints. headings.title: Limitation period for loaned property damage or loss actions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1991 history note, and July 1, 1992 effective date. Bars damage actions against a museum for injury to or loss of loaned property after the earlier of two years from museum notice or five years from the injury or loss.

headings.title: Limitation period for actions to recover loaned property
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and July 1, 1992 effective-date note. Bars recovery actions against a museum after the earlier of one year from termination or undocumented-property title notice or five years from filing a preservation notice.

headings.title: Deemed donation upon failure to bring timely recovery action
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and July 1, 1992 effective-date note. Deems loaned property donated to the museum if the lender or claimant fails to file a recovery action within the periods specified in subsections 1 and 2.

headings.title: Purchaser title based on museum title representation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and July 1, 1992 effective-date note. Provides that a purchaser from a museum acquires good and valid title if the museum represents that it acquired title pursuant to sections 184.101 to 184.122.

headings.title: Recovery or value remedy when notice was not given
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and July 1, 1992 effective-date note. Operates notwithstanding subsections 3 and 4 to let an unnotified lender or claimant who proves museum receipt of a compliant section 184.114 preservation notice within the preceding seven years recover the property or its disposition value plus legal interest.

headings.title: Museum immunity for returning property and competing claims
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and July 1, 1992 effective-date note. Protects museums from liability for returning property to the original lender absent a court order or to an uncontested claimant showing reasonable proof under section 184.114, placing the equity-action burden on competing claimants.

headings.title: Effective date for section 184.116
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and 1991 history note. Sets July 1, 1992 as the delayed effective date for section 184.116.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all seven subsections, 1991 history, and July 1, 1992 delayed effective-date note, and verified all fingerprints. headings.title: Twenty-five-year museum record retention requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in, subdivisions (1)-(4), and paragraphs (4)(a)-(f) plus 1991 history note. Requires museums on or after December 31, 1991 to retain originals or accurate copies of preservation notices, loan/delivery receipts or ledgers, and specified party and transaction records for at least twenty-five years.

headings.title: Director rulemaking on minimum museum recordkeeping
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1991 history note. Authorizes the director of economic development to determine by rule the minimum form and substance of museum recordkeeping under sections 184.101 to 184.122.

headings.title: Lender or claimant duty to report address or ownership changes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1991 history note. Requires lenders and claimants of loaned property to notify the museum of address or ownership changes, noting failure may result in loss of property rights.

headings.title: Filing preservation notice and limits on claim validation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1991 history note. headings.title: Dual-majority approval, effective date, certification, and resubmission bar

headings.title: Payment of election costs under sections 115.063 and 115.065
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1969-1989 history notes. Directs that election costs be paid as provided in sections 115.063 and 115.065.

headings.title: Board request and chapter 115 notice for tax increase

headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text including ballot table and 1979-1989 history notes. Prescribes the ballot question for increasing the St. Louis Science Center subdistrict tax rate up to six cents per $100 assessed valuation, set annually by the board based on approved budgets.

headings.title: Dual-majority approval, effective date, certification, costs, and resubmission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1979-1989 history notes. headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and section notes. Authorizes DOR refunds and dishonored-check redemptions from trust fund receipts, requires ninety-day county notice before repealing the tax, permits one-year two-percent retention for post-repeal refunds before closing the account, and mandates district notification.

headings.title: County withdrawal procedure, ninety-day delay, and continuing obligations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and section notes. Permits an eligible county to withdraw by resolution and majority voter approval plus formal written notice to other member counties, with actual withdrawal taking effect ninety days after notice is sent and without relieving the county of assumed or incurred obligations including outstanding bonded debt.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all seven subsections including the ballot table, subsection 2's continuation paragraph, 2010 history note, and 2013 Page v. Scavuzzo annotation (412 S.W.3d 263, holding the county commission has discretion whether to place a petition question on the ballot), and verified all fingerprints. Checked the charter-county collection precondition, retained source quirks ('with the district' in 2, 'such subdistrict' and 'sections 184.500 to 184.515' in 3), DOR trust fund/refund/abolition provisions, and withdrawal terms. Revised subsection 7 to 'County withdrawal procedure, ninety-day delay, and continuing obligations' to reflect the post-notice effective delay and full obligation scope; retained subsections 1-6.

headings.title: Kansas City Zoological District commission membership and selection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in, subdivisions (1)-(4), and paragraphs (4)(a)-(b) plus 2010 history note. Constitutes the commission as a corporate political subdivision comprising one county governing-body member per member county, one Kansas City parks board member, the Kansas City zoo executive director, and one member per establishing county selected from three Friends of the Zoo, Inc. nominees (majority vote in charter counties, unanimous vote in noncharter counties).

headings.title: Commissioner terms, withdrawal termination, vacancies, and removal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2010 history note. Sets initial and successor term lengths and office-tied expirations for each commissioner class, terminates a withdrawing county's seats upon effective withdrawal, transfers the zoo director's seat automatically, fills vacancies by original manner, and allows removal for cause by the appointing authority.

headings.title: Annual selection of commission officers and treasurer bond
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2010 history note. Directs the commission annually to select a chairperson, vice chairperson, and bonded treasurer from its membership.

headings.title: Appointment, duties, and compensation of commission staff
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 2010 history note. Authorizes the commission to appoint officers, agents, and employees and determine their qualifications, duties, and compensation.

headings.title: Open public meetings within district and public notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and 2010 history note. Requires the commission to set meeting times and places within the district, hold open public meetings, and provide public notice.

headings.title: Quorum, voting, tie-breaking vote, and fourteen-day agenda notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and 2010 history note. Defines a majority quorum and majority-present voting, grants the Kansas City zoo executive director a tie-breaking vote, and requires a written agenda mailed by first-class mail at least fourteen calendar days before binding action.

headings.title: Conflict-of-interest disclosure, abstention, and zoo director exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and 2010 history note. Subjects commissioners to state conflict-of-interest laws requiring written disclosure and abstention, while exempting the Kansas City zoo executive director from abstaining on matters relating to the Kansas City zoo.

headings.title: Common-law official immunity, indemnification, and legal defense
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 text and 2010 history note (retaining archived 'cost of expense' phrasing). Grants commissioners common-law official immunity for acts or omissions in official duties and requires full indemnification and defense at commission expense.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all eight subsections including subdivisions (1)(1)-(4) and paragraphs (4)(a)-(b) plus 2010 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Verified charter-county majority versus noncharter-county unanimous appointment rules, withdrawal seat termination, KC zoo director tie-breaking vote and conflict-of-interest abstention exception, fourteen-day mailed agenda rule, and common-law official immunity/indemnification (retaining source 'cost of expense' phrasing in subsection 8). Retained all eight titles as accurate.

headings.title: Corporate powers, zoological facilities, and grants or donations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2010 history note. Authorizes adopting a seal and bylaws, contracting, suing and being sued, acquiring, operating, maintaining, and disposing of zoological facilities within the district, and receiving public appropriations, donations, and grants.

headings.title: Borrowing after five years, voter-approved bonds, refunding, and security
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(4) plus 2010 history note (retaining archived 'under this compact' wording in (3)). Beginning five years after district creation, authorizes borrowing via voter-approved notes/bonds, refunding obligations capped at principal and accrued interest, pledges of sales tax/admissions/other revenues and property mortgages or deeds of trust, and holder covenants.

headings.title: Support for zoological activities and decision factors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(6) plus 2010 history note. Authorizes donations, contributions, grants, and other support—financial or otherwise—for zoological activities in member counties, directing consideration of six factors led by supporting the Kansas City zoo's maintenance and operation.

headings.title: Commissioners' actual and necessary official-duty expenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 2010 history note. Authorizes the commission to provide for actual and necessary expenses of commissioners incurred in performing official duties.

headings.title: Annual operations report submission and county newspaper publication
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and 2010 history note. Requires preparing an annual operations and transactions report submitted to member/appointing counties, the Kansas City parks board, and Friends of the Zoo, Inc., and publishing it in each member county's official newspaper.

headings.title: Necessary and incidental commission powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and 2010 history note. Grants necessary and incidental functions and powers not inconsistent with the Missouri constitution or laws.

headings.title: Exclusion of Kansas City zoo management and land control
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and 2010 history note. Clarifies that section 184.509 grants no authority to manage the Kansas City zoo or retain title to or control over lands occupied by the zoo.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all seven subsections including subdivisions (2)(1)-(4) and (3)(1)-(6) plus 2010 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Verified five-year post-creation waiting period for borrowing, retained 'under this compact' phrasing in 2(3), financial-or-otherwise support scope in 3, expense provision in 4, annual report recipients/publication in 5, and KC zoo management/land exclusion in 7. Revised subsections 2 (adding 'after five years'), 3 (broadening from 'Financial support' to 'Support'), and 4 (neutral 'official-duty expenses' phrasing); retained subsections 1, 5, 6, and 7.

headings.title: Initial six-month county funding and ongoing sales tax funding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2010 history note. Requires member counties to appropriate administrative funding for the first six months after district creation, with subsequent funding drawn from the section 184.503 sales tax fund.

headings.title: Debt and county credit limits and political subdivision budget
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2010 history note. Bars incurring indebtedness or pledging member county credit except as authorized in section 184.509 and requires budget preparation, adoption, and publication as for other political subdivisions.

headings.title: Accounting records, annual public accountant audit, and report
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2010 history note. Requires accurate accounts of receipts and disbursements, yearly audit by a certified or licensed public accountant, and inclusion of the audit report in the commission's annual report.

headings.title: Inspection of commission accounts by authorized representatives
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 2010 history note. Opens commission accounts at reasonable times for inspection by representatives of member counties, cities appointing a commissioner (retained as archived), the Friends of the Zoo, Inc. executive committee, and others authorized by the commission.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and 2010 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Checked six-month county funding transition to section 184.503 sales tax fund, section 184.509 debt/credit exception, annual certified or licensed public accountant audit included in the annual report, and account inspection rights (retaining archived 'cities that appoint a commissioner' phrasing in subsection 4). Revised subsection 3 to 'Accounting records, annual public accountant audit, and report' to remove the unstated qualifier 'independent' and cover annual-report inclusion; retained subsections 1, 2, and 4.

headings.title: City formation, boundaries, voter petition, notice, and tax cap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1990 history note (retaining archived cross-reference to section 184.602 for adjacent areas petitioning and voting to join, though voting procedures appear in subsections 2, 4, and 6 of section 184.600). Authorizes a metropolitan zoo district in a city of 100,000+ inhabitants in a non-adjoining first class county upon five-percent voter petition (not held before 1992), sixty-day newspaper notice, up to ten-cent tax per $100 valuation, and boundaries including annexed lands and joining adjacent areas.

headings.title: Petition and election for adjacent areas within two miles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1990 history note. Allows residents in a first class county within two miles of an eligible city to petition the county commission with five percent of area voters to vote on joining the district at the city's tax rate.

headings.title: Ballot form for city metropolitan zoo district election
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text including ballot table and 1990 history note. Prescribes the ballot proposition for establishing a metropolitan zoo district and tax rate within the city.

headings.title: Ballot form for outside-city area to join district
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text including ballot table and 1990 history note. Prescribes the ballot proposition for an outside-city area to become part of a metropolitan zoo district with the city and levy the district tax.

headings.title: City election approval, effective date, certification, and resubmission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and 1990 history note. Establishes the district and tax rate effective January 1 of the next year upon majority city vote, requires thirty-day city certification, and bars resubmission within one year after rejection.

headings.title: Outside-city election approval, city prerequisite, and resubmission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and 1990 history note. Adds an outside-city area effective January 1 of the next year upon majority area vote provided city voters voted to form the district, requires thirty-day county certification, and bars resubmission within one year.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all six subsections including both ballot tables and 1990 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Checked city population/non-adjoining first-class-county criteria, post-1992 election floor, ten-cent tax cap, retained cross-reference to section 184.602 in subsection 1, two-mile adjacent-area petitions, and city-formation prerequisite in subsection 6. Revised subsection 4 to 'Ballot form for outside-city area to join district' to avoid conflating district membership with municipal annexation; retained subsections 1-3, 5, and 6.

headings.title: City board appointments, staggered terms, qualifications, and officers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1990 history note. Provides for nine uncompensated city board members appointed by the mayor with city council approval for three-year terms (staggered 1-3 years initially), one-year city voter/residency qualifications, vacancy filling, officer elections, and bylaws.

headings.title: Proportional board representation for outside-city joining areas
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1990 history note. Grants outside-city areas voting to join the district at least one representative and proportional county-commission-appointed three-year representatives calculated by the county clerk from city census population divided by nine.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 1990 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Checked nine-member mayor-appointed/council-approved city board terms and one-year voter/residency qualifications versus county-clerk census-quotient proportional representation and county-commission appointments for outside-city joining areas. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Board request and chapter 115 notice for tax rate increase
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1990 history note. Authorizes the metropolitan zoo district board to request city election officials to submit a maximum tax rate increase above section 184.600 to district voters with chapter 115 legal notice.

headings.title: Ballot form for metropolitan zoo district tax increase
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text including ballot table and 1990 history note. Prescribes the ballot question for replacing the district's current tax rate with a higher maximum rate per $100 assessed valuation.

headings.title: Majority approval, effective date, certification, and resubmission bar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1990 history note. Makes an approved new tax rate effective January 1 of the following year, requires thirty-day city election certification, and bars resubmission within one year of rejection.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including the ballot table and 1990 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Verified section 184.600 cross-reference, chapter 115 legal notice, January 1 effective date, thirty-day city certification, and one-year resubmission bar. Retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: General property, exhibit, and service contracting powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1990 history note. Authorizes each metropolitan zoo district to own, lease, acquire, sell, and control real, personal, or mixed property and exhibits and contract for district services.

headings.title: Transfer of public zoo property, city conditions, and voter-approved fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1990 history note. Vests existing public zoos in the city or owned by the city and related obligations in the district, subject to a ninety-day city option to deed or contract for conveyance on city-specified conditions, and preserves the right to continue charging voter-approved fees.

headings.title: District staffing and transferred employee benefit protections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1990 history note. Authorizes employing necessary personnel and transfers existing publicly owned zoo employees to the district with equal or better seniority, pension, compensation, and fringe benefits insofar as possible.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and 1990 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Checked repeated 'lease' text in subsection 1, existing public zoo vesting and ninety-day city option to set deed/conveyance conditions plus voter-approved fee continuation in subsection 2, and employee transfer protections ('insofar as may be possible') in subsection 3. Revised subsection 2 to 'Transfer of public zoo property, city conditions, and voter-approved fees' for fuller scope and clarity; retained subsections 1 and 3.

headings.title: Voter petition to dissolve metropolitan zoo district
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1990 history note. Permits dissolution of a district formed under sections 184.600 to 184.622 upon filing a petition signed by eight percent of gubernatorial voters with the district governing body for submission under formation procedures.

headings.title: Ballot form for metropolitan zoo district dissolution
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text including ballot table and 1990 history note. Prescribes the ballot question for dissolving a metropolitan zoo district.

headings.title: Majority dissolution vote, certification, and election costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1990 history note. Dissolves the district upon majority 'YES' vote, requires thirty-day election certification to city or county chief executives, and assigns election costs to the city and county as provided by law.

headings.title: Dissolution under section 67.955 and reversion of city property
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1990 history note. Requires carrying out dissolution under section 67.955 except that city-owned property donated to the district under section 184.606(2) reverts to the city.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections including the dissolution ballot table and 1990 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Checked sections 184.600 to 184.622 applicability, eight-percent voter petition, majority approval, city/county certification and election costs, and section 67.955 dissolution with section 184.606(2) donated city property reversion. Retained all four titles as accurate.

headings.title: Debt-retirement property tax levy for section 184.612 debt
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1990 history note. Requires the district board, before incurring section 184.612 indebtedness, to provide for an annual tangible-property tax sufficient to pay principal and interest and retire the debt within twenty years, in addition to sections 184.600 and 184.604 levies.

headings.title: Submission of additional indebtedness question to district voters
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1990 history note. Directs the district board to submit the question of incurring section 184.612 additional indebtedness to district voters.

headings.title: Ballot form for metropolitan zoo district bond issue
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text including indented ballot form and 1990 history note. Prescribes substantial ballot wording for submitting a district bond issue amount and purpose.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including indented bond ballot form and 1990 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Checked twenty-year debt-retirement levy prerequisite before incurring section 184.612 indebtedness (in addition to sections 184.600 and 184.604 levies) and voter submission requirement. Revised subsection 1 to 'Debt-retirement property tax levy for section 184.612 debt' to preserve the exact cross-reference and conditional trigger; retained subsections 2 and 3.

headings.title: General definitions for Missouri Museum and Cultural District Act
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(6) plus 1997/2013 history notes. Defines 'board', 'cultural asset', 'disaster area' (requiring Presidential Stafford Act declaration and municipal redevelopment ordinance within three years), 'district', 'museum', and 'owner of real property' for sections 184.800 to 184.880.

headings.title: Definitions of required majority and qualified voters
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(2) plus 1997/2013 history notes. Defines 'approval of the required majority' (simple majority) and 'qualified voters' (real property owners within the proposed district) for Article X, Sections 11(c), 16, and 22, section 137.073, and sections 184.800 to 184.880.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions (1)(1)-(6) and (2)(1)-(2) plus 1997/2013 history notes, and verified all fingerprints. Verified Missouri Museum and Cultural District Act short title (section 184.800), Stafford Act/three-year redevelopment-ordinance disaster-area definition, and Article X/section 137.073 qualified-voter and simple-majority definitions. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Disaster-area eligibility and authorized museum or cultural projects
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1997-2013 history notes. Permits creating a district where the majority of property lies within a disaster area to fund, promote, plan, design, construct, improve, maintain, and operate museum and cultural asset projects.

headings.title: Political subdivision status of district
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1997-2013 history notes. Declares a museum and cultural district to be a political subdivision of the state.

headings.title: Prohibition on naming district structures for commercial ventures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1998/2013 history notes. Prohibits naming any structure operated by a museum and cultural district board under sections 184.800 to 184.880 for a commercial venture.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and 1997-2013 history notes, and verified all fingerprints. Verified majority-in-disaster-area eligibility, museum and cultural asset project purposes, political subdivision status, and commercial-venture structure-naming prohibition. Retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: Two-thirds property-owner petition, venue, and fifteen-year deadline
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1997-2019 (S.B. 397) history notes. Permits owners of at least two-thirds of real property in a proposed district to file a circuit court creation petition in the county within fifteen years after the Presidential disaster declaration.

headings.title: Permitted parcel contiguity and municipal overlap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1997-2019 history notes. Allows a proposed district to contain one or more contiguous or noncontiguous real property parcels and include portions of one or more municipalities.

headings.title: Required contents of district creation petition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 including lead-in and subdivisions (1)-(4) plus 1997-2019 history notes. Requires listing all property owners' names and addresses, specific boundaries and map, general purpose with museum/cultural asset descriptions and operation plans, and proposed district name.

headings.title: Service on nonjoining property owners and answer deadline
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1997-2019 history notes. Requires serving named nonjoining property owners who do not enter appearance and waive service under supreme court rules and raising objections by timely answer.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections including subdivisions (3)(1)-(4) and 1997-2019 (S.B. 397) history notes, and verified all fingerprints. Verified two-thirds real property owner threshold, circuit court venue, fifteen-year post-Presidential-declaration filing deadline, contiguous/noncontiguous parcel and municipal overlap rules, petition contents, and supreme court rule service/answer provisions. Retained all four titles as accurate.

headings.title: Property owner filings supporting or opposing district creation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1997/2013 history note. Allows any real property owner in the proposed district to join or file a supporting petition or an opposing answer seeking judgment on those issues.

headings.title: Nonjury circuit court hearing and incorporation judgment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1997/2013 history note. Requires a nonjury hearing; directs refusing incorporation if the petition is defective or district/plan is unconstitutional, and otherwise declaring the district organized and approving its operation plan.

headings.title: Right to appeal final incorporation or refusal orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1997/2013 history note. Allows any party who filed a petition or answer to appeal circuit court orders refusing or granting incorporation as final judgments.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and 1997/2013 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Checked property-owner supporting/opposing filings, nonjury hearing standard for petition defects or unconstitutionality, and final-judgment appeal rights for both refusal and incorporation orders. Retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: Published notice and meeting to elect initial directors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1997/2013 history note (retaining archived 'shall, give notice' punctuation). Directs the circuit clerk within thirty days of a final organization order to publish two consecutive weekly notices (last at least ten days before meeting) calling a property-owner meeting to elect five directors who are owners or owner representatives.

headings.title: Meeting organization, acreage-based voting, and proxy voting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1997/2013 history note. Directs assembled property owners to elect a meeting chairman and secretary, grants one vote in person or by proxy per acre owned for each director, and states directors need not be legal voters.

headings.title: Three-year director terms, successor elections, and interim vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1997/2013 history note. Establishes three-year terms until successors qualify, board-called owner meetings for successor elections, and authority of remaining directors to elect an interim director for resignation or disqualification vacancies.

headings.title: Minimum age qualification for directors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1997/2013 history note. Requires district directors to be at least twenty-one years of age.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and 1997/2013 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Verified thirty-day circuit clerk notice ('shall, give notice' punctuation retained), two-week publication and ten-day pre-meeting rule, five-director election by owners/representatives, one-vote-per-acre in-person/proxy voting, non-voter eligibility, three-year terms/vacancies, and age-twenty-one requirement. Retained all four titles as accurate.

headings.title: Board legislative and executive powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1997/2013 history note. Vests all legislative and executive powers of the museum and cultural district in its board of directors.

headings.title: Initial board meeting, officer elections, and dual-office limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1997/2013 history note. Requires meeting within thirty days after initial election, electing a chairman, secretary, treasurer, and other officers from board members initially and after each election, and prohibits one director from serving as both chairman and secretary.

headings.title: Defining district fiscal years and adopting corporate seal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1997/2013 history note. Directs the board at its first meeting to define first and subsequent fiscal years by resolution and adopt a corporate seal.

headings.title: Board quorum and simple-majority voting threshold
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1997/2013 history note. Establishes a simple majority of the board as a quorum and allows a simple majority of those voting to act and approve board resolutions.

headings.title: Director time commitment and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and 1997/2013 history note. Directs directors to devote time required for faithful discharge of duties and permits reimbursing actual expenditures incurred on behalf of the district.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections and 1997/2013 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Verified legislative/executive powers, thirty-day initial meeting, officer elections and chairman/secretary dual-office ban, fiscal year resolution and corporate seal, simple-majority quorum/voting, and time/expense provisions. Retained all five titles as accurate.

headings.title: Authorized district funding sources and project uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1997-2013 history notes (retaining archived 'which is reasonably connected' wording and dual section ranges 184.840-184.880 and 184.800-184.880). Authorizes receiving and spending funds from authorized methods and federal, state, local, or private sources for museum, cultural asset, and connected educational program purposes.

headings.title: Authorized general revenue appropriations for twenty years after 2013
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2013 S.B. 23 history note. Authorizes the general assembly to make annual general revenue appropriations to a sections 184.800 to 184.880 district for a period of twenty years after January 1, 2013.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and 1997-2013 history notes, and verified all fingerprints. Checked authorized uses/sources (retaining 'which is reasonably connected' wording and dual section ranges 184.840-184.880 and 184.800-184.880 in subsection 1) and twenty-year post-January 1, 2013 permissive general revenue appropriation window in subsection 2. Revised subsection 2 to 'Authorized general revenue appropriations for twenty years after 2013' to preserve the statutory anchor date; retained subsection 1.

headings.title: Board resolution and optional voter submission for sales tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1997/2013 history note. Authorizes the district board by resolution to impose a retail sales tax on sections 144.010 to 144.525 sales for designated museum or cultural purposes and permits submitting the question to qualified property-owner voters using board-election voting interests.

headings.title: Effective date of museum and cultural district sales tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1997/2013 history note. Makes the sales tax effective on the first day of the second calendar quarter following adoption by the board or by qualified voters if submitted.

headings.title: Retailer collection of sales tax as part of price
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1997/2013 history note. Requires district retailers to add the sales tax to the sale price as a debt of the purchaser recoverable at law like the purchase price.

headings.title: District authority to establish sales tax collection brackets
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1997/2013 history note. Allows the district to establish penny-fraction brackets for sellers in lieu of section 144.285 brackets without altering reporting or remitting duties.

headings.title: Special trust fund deposit, dedicated use, and fund investment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and 1997/2013 history note. Requires depositing designated sales tax revenues into a special trust fund restricted solely to the designated museum or cultural purpose, with board investment authority for unneeded funds.

headings.title: Permitted sales tax rates and district-wide uniformity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and 1997/2013 history note. Authorizes uniform district-wide sales tax rates of one-half, three-fourths, or one percent on retail sales taxable under sections 144.010 to 144.525.

headings.title: District administration, collection, enforcement, and rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and 1997/2013 history note. Assigns the district all functions incident to administering, collecting, enforcing, and operating the sales tax on district-prescribed forms and administrative rules (in unresolved statutory tension with DOR collection provisions in subsection 8).

headings.title: Incorporated state tax laws, DOR collection, and trust fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 text and 1997/2013 history note (retaining archived 'Missouri Museum Cultural District Tax Fund' name, trailing 'credit of such county' wording, and tension with district collection in subsections 7 and 13). Incorporates sections 144.010-144.525, 32.085, 32.087, and 32.057, creates a non-state special trust fund for DOR-collected revenue less a one-percent general-revenue fee, and authorizes DOR refunds and dishonored-check redemptions.

headings.title: Incorporation of state sales tax exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 9 text and 1997/2013 history note. Makes all exemptions granted under sections 144.010 to 144.525 applicable to the district sales tax.

headings.title: Validity of state permits and optional district exemption form
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 10 text and 1997/2013 history note. Treats state sales tax permits, exemption certificates, and retail certificates under sections 144.010 to 144.525 as sufficient, while allowing the district to prescribe a district exemption certificate form.

headings.title: Incorporation of state confidentiality and sales tax penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 11 text and 1997/2013 history note. Applies penalties in section 32.057 and sections 144.010 to 144.525 to violations of section 184.845.

headings.title: Sourcing rules for retail sales except motor vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 12 text and 1997/2013 history note. Deems retail sales (excluding motor vehicles) consummated at the retailer's place of business—or initial-order location for multi-location retailers or employee work location—unless delivered out of state.

headings.title: District deposit, revenue records, inspection, and return confidentiality
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 13 text and 1997/2013 history note. Requires depositing district-collected sales taxes in a special fund, maintaining records open to district officers, directors, and DOR, and keeping business tax returns confidential like state sales tax returns.

headings.title: Limit on repealing or amending tax if repayment impaired
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 14 text and 1997/2013 history note. Prohibits repealing or amending a district sales tax unless doing so will not impair the district's ability to repay incurred liabilities, borrowed funds, or revenue bonds, notes, or other project obligations.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all fourteen subsections and 1997/2013 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Audited the statutory tension between district administration/collection in subsection 7 (and district deposit in subsection 13) versus DOR collection, one-percent state fee, and non-state Missouri Museum Cultural District Tax Fund in subsection 8 (retaining trailing 'credit of such county' phrasing without reconciling). Revised subsection 8 to 'Incorporated state tax laws, DOR collection, and trust fund' to avoid calling the explicitly non-state fund a 'state trust fund', and revised subsection 14 to 'Limit on repealing or amending tax if repayment impaired' to reflect the impairment test rather than a flat debt bar; retained subsections 1-7 and 9-13.

headings.title: Board resolution, one-dollar cap, and optional voter submission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2013 S.B. 23 history note. Authorizes a district admissions fee up to one dollar per seat or admission sold on commercial or nonprofit events or venues in addition to taxes, with optional submission to qualified voters specifying covered event or venue types.

headings.title: Effective date following voter adoption of admission fee
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2013 history note. Makes the admission fee effective on the first day of the second calendar quarter following adoption by the qualified voters (retaining tension with subsection 1's permissive 'may submit' language).

headings.title: Special trust fund deposit, dedicated use, and fund investment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2013 history note. Requires depositing admission fee revenues into a special trust fund restricted solely to the designated museum or cultural purpose, with board investment authority for unneeded funds.

headings.title: District administration, collection, enforcement, forms, and rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 2013 history note. Assigns the district all administration, collection, enforcement, and operation functions for the admission fee under district-prescribed forms and administrative rules and regulations.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and 2013 S.B. 23 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Verified one-dollar per-seat/admission cap, optional voter submission in subsection 1 versus voter-adoption effective date in subsection 2 (retained faithfully), dedicated special trust fund in subsection 3, and district administration/collection/forms/rules in subsection 4. Revised subsection 4 to 'District administration, collection, enforcement, forms, and rules' to include administrative rules; retained subsections 1-3.

headings.title: Authority to contract and incur obligations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1997/2013 history note. Authorizes a museum and cultural district to contract and incur obligations appropriate to accomplish its purposes.

headings.title: Authority to enter leases and lease-purchase agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1997/2013 history note. Authorizes entering lease or lease-purchase agreements for necessary or convenient real or personal property.

headings.title: Operating and management agreements for museums and cultural assets
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1997/2013 history note. Authorizes operating and management agreements to operate a museum or cultural asset or carry out other authorized district functions.

headings.title: Authority to borrow money at district-determined rates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1997/2013 history note. Authorizes borrowing money for district purposes at interest rates determined by the district.

headings.title: Issuing and securing bonds, notes, and intergovernmental financing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and 1997/2013 history note. Authorizes issuing bonds, notes, and obligations secured by mortgages, pledges, assignments, security agreements, or deeds of trust subject to sections 184.800 to 184.880, and securing bond financing through another political subdivision or state agency.

headings.title: Labor agreements, bidding, contract awards, and construction supervision
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and 1997/2013 history note. Authorizes entering labor agreements, setting bid conditions, awarding contracts, paying contractors, and supervising construction of museum or cultural asset projects.

headings.title: Hiring staff and incidental ownership, operation, and maintenance powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and 1997/2013 history note. Authorizes hiring employees, entering leases and contracts, and taking actions necessary or incidental to owning, operating, and maintaining each district museum and cultural asset.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all seven subsections and 1997/2013 history note, and verified all fingerprints. Checked contracting, lease/lease-purchase, operating/management agreements, borrowing, secured bonds/intergovernmental financing subject to sections 184.800 to 184.880, labor/bidding/construction supervision, and hiring/incidental powers. Retained all seven titles as accurate and distinct.

headings.title: Issuance, security, maturity, terms, and sale of revenue bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1997 history note, and July 7, 1997 effective date. Authorizes board-resolution revenue bonds maturing in up to forty years payable from district revenues and pledged property without first-bond priority, operating notwithstanding section 108.170 and permitting public or private sale.

headings.title: Authority and methods for issuing refunding bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and July 7, 1997 effective-date note. Authorizes refunding outstanding district bonds (up to principal, unpaid interest, premiums, fees, and expenses) by sale or holder-consented exchange regardless of maturity date, project, or serial terms.

headings.title: Exclusive district liability and mandatory bond face disclaimer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and July 7, 1997 effective-date note. Limits bond liability exclusively to the district and pledged funds—excluding the state and other agencies or political subdivisions—and requires a corresponding disclaimer on the face of every bond.

headings.title: State tax exemption with state estate tax exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and July 7, 1997 effective-date note. Exempts section 184.860 bonds, interest, and proceeds from Missouri taxation for all purposes except the state estate tax.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections, 1997 history note, and July 7, 1997 effective-date note, and verified all fingerprints. Checked forty-year maturity cap, notwithstanding section 108.170 terms, public/private sale, refunding limits and exchange consent, exclusive district liability/mandatory face disclaimer, and Missouri tax exemption with state estate tax exception. Retained all four titles as accurate.

headings.title: District liability and property insurance charged to project
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1997 history note, and July 7, 1997 effective date. Authorizes obtaining liability insurance for the district, officers, and employees (considering legal liability limits) and real/personal property loss insurance, with costs charged against the project.

headings.title: Contractor and operator liability insurance naming district insureds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and July 7, 1997 effective-date note. Permits requiring construction, maintenance, operational, and management contractors to carry liability insurance naming the district, its directors, and employees as additional named insureds.

headings.title: Conditions and feasibility standard for district self-insurance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and July 7, 1997 effective-date note. Bars self-insuring unless the district finds sufficient funds to cover anticipated judgments or settlements without interrupting project completion, and permits self-insurance if liability coverage is not economically feasible.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections, 1997 history note, and July 7, 1997 effective-date note, and verified all fingerprints. Verified project-charged liability/property insurance, contractor/operator additional-named-insured authority, and self-insurance sufficiency and economic-feasibility conditions. Retained all three titles as accurate.
